Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a large gas-filled structure with an air-fluid level in the right hemithorax and an indistinct right diaphragm, which is characteristic of bowel herniating into the chest (diaphragmatic hernia). The rapid expansion of this gas collection causing respiratory distress indicates tension gastrothorax, distinguishing it from pneumothorax or simple effusion.
